html:
In August 1866 the General Sherman, an armed American merchant ship, sailed up the Taedong River to Pyongyang, now in North Korea, to demand trade, and was burned with all its crew killed.

Joseon Korea was then closed to Western trade, and that year its regent was also killing Catholic converts. The ship ignored orders to leave, took an official hostage and fired on crowds. When it ran aground, local people and soldiers set it on fire. A Welsh missionary, Robert Jermain Thomas, died with the crew.

The United States sent a punitive expedition in 1871, which Korea repelled. Korea was opened only by the Treaty of Ganghwa with Japan in 1876. North Korea teaches that Kim Il Sung's great-grandfather led the attack, and moors the captured USS Pueblo nearby.
